newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Manila stocks finished higher on Thursday in quiet trade as most investors were sidelined by the Christmas holidays, traders said.
"The market was up but in thin volume as most people are in vacation mode. Everyone's looking at 1997," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.
The main index closed 12.99 points, or 0.41 percent, up at 3,165.52 points.
The volume of shares traded was 2.326 billion valued at 1.489 billion pesos. All sectors ended up with only the oil sector bucking the trend.
PLDT provided excitement to Thursday's session as it closed $2.25 higher on Wall Street on Tuesday at $53 7/8. The stock gained 25 pesos to 1,425 pesos a share by the end of trading.
Traders said news in the morning that President Fidel Ramos checked out of the hospital three days after a critical surgery also perked up the market.

"We may see a bit more excitement tommorrow since it's the last trading day and the market may want to end up on a happy note and do more window-dressing," Russell Ong, analyst at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc said.
Traders said the index will likely end higher tomorrow compared to the 2,594.18 points close of the last trading day in 1995.
Liu added the Philippine equities market may see more volatility next year due to political developments such as the 1998 presidential elections.
